issues.legal_issue: The English doctrine of conversion does not give a purchaser equitable ownership of immovable property under Indian law, although a contract may create an enforceable obligation annexed to ownership.
material_facts: The dispute arose from an agreement concerning immovable property.
The agreement provided for the property to be sold to the purchaser or, in an alternative circumstance, sold at auction with the surplus paid to the purchaser.
issues.conclusion: The English doctrine of conversion cannot be bodily applied in India, where an agreement to sell immovable property does not itself create an interest in the property. It creates an obligation annexed to ownership that may be enforced against a transferee with notice or a gratuitous transferee.
issues.legal_principle: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, sections 40 and 54, distinguish an enforceable obligation annexed to ownership from an interest in the property. The Court relied on Rambaran Prasad v. Ram Mohit Hazra and Narandas Karsondas v. S.A. Kamtam in rejecting dual legal and equitable ownership under Indian law. Equity may assist in interpreting Indian statutes that incorporate equitable principles, but the English doctrine of conversion cannot be transplanted wholesale.

predicates.indian_immovable_property_contract_dispu: The proceeding concerns the legal effect under Indian law of an agreement concerning immovable property.
predicates.agreement_to_sell_property: A party agreed to transfer immovable property to another person.

issues.definition: When a dispute under Indian law concerns an agreement to sell immovable property, the agreement creates an enforceable obligation rather than equitable ownership in the property.

issues.legal_issue: A contractual duty to auction property and pay the purchaser any surplus is an obligation in the nature of a trust that may be specifically enforced.
material_facts: The purchaser had paid part of the agreed price in advance.
The owner was bound to sell the property at auction if the purchaser did not complete the purchase.
The owner had to pay the purchaser any auction proceeds exceeding the stipulated price, and the advance payment was to be credited.
issues.conclusion: The owner's obligation to auction the property and pay any surplus to the purchaser was an obligation annexed to ownership, in the nature of a trust, and could be specifically enforced.
issues.legal_principle: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, sections 40 and 54, provide for an obligation annexed to ownership without creating an interest in the property. Indian Trusts Act, 1882, section 94, requires a person in possession who does not hold the whole beneficial interest to hold the property for the benefit of those entitled to that interest to the extent of their just demands. The Specific Relief Act, 1877, section 12(a), permits specific performance where the agreed act is wholly or partly performance of a trust; section 16 permits specific performance of a severable part of a contract that can and ought to be performed.

predicates.contract_enforcement_suit: A person brings a proceeding to enforce an obligation under a contract concerning property.
predicates.owner_must_auction_if_purchase_not_compl: The agreement requires the owner to sell the property by auction if the purchaser does not complete the purchase.
predicates.owner_must_pay_surplus_to_purchaser: The agreement requires the owner to pay the purchaser any sale proceeds exceeding the amount due to the owner.

issues.definition: If a contract-enforcement suit concerns an agreement requiring an auction when purchase is not completed and payment of any surplus to the purchaser, that auction-and-surplus obligation may be specifically enforced.

issues.legal_issue: An obligation under a contract should not be denied specific enforcement where monetary compensation is not determinable on the evidence.
material_facts: The purchaser sought enforcement of the contractual obligation to sell the property by auction and account for the proceeds.
The owner did not raise an appropriate plea or provide evidence establishing suitable compensation.
The nature and terms of the agreement made the amount of compensation or damages indeterminable.
issues.conclusion: The contractual obligation should be specifically enforced because compensation or damages were not determinable.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principles governing specific relief, including the Specific Relief Act, 1877, provisions on specific performance and contracts not specifically enforceable. On the contract's terms and the evidence, monetary compensation was not determinable; the owner had neither properly pleaded that issue nor proved suitable compensation.

predicates.specific_performance_claim: A claimant seeks a court order requiring performance of a contractual obligation.
predicates.monetary_compensation_not_determinable: The contract's nature, terms, and circumstances do not make suitable monetary compensation determinable.
predicates.no_evidence_establishes_suitable_compens: The opposing party provides no evidence establishing an amount of suitable compensation.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks specific performance and suitable monetary compensation is not determinable or proved, the contractual obligation may be specifically enforced.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser does not lose contractual rights by declining an optional purchase or by bona fide claiming statutory tenant protections that are later found unavailable.
material_facts: The agreement gave the purchaser the option to buy the property but did not require the purchaser to do so.
The agreement provided for an auction if the purchaser did not buy the property.
The purchaser resisted delivery of possession while claiming statutory tenant protections in a bona fide belief that they applied.
The court later found that the purchaser was not entitled to those statutory protections.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser did not default by declining to buy the property and could not be denied contractual rights for having bona fide claimed statutory protections that were found unavailable.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the agreement as giving the purchaser an option, not imposing an obligation, to buy the property. It also held that a person who bona fide claims the benefit of social legislation should not lose contractual rights when found not entitled to the statutory benefit.

predicates.contract_enforcement_suit: A person brings a proceeding to enforce contractual rights.
predicates.purchase_was_optional: The agreement allowed the purchaser to buy the property but did not require the purchaser to do so.
predicates.purchaser_bona_fide_claimed_unavailable_: The purchaser resisted the other party's claim in a bona fide belief that statutory protections applied, but those protections were later found unavailable.

issues.definition: In a contractual enforcement proceeding, a purchaser retains contractual rights if purchase was optional and the purchaser bona fide claimed statutory protection that proved unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: Temporary statutory restrictions on land alienation do not bar enforcement of an earlier contract when the relevant statutory restriction no longer applies at the time the contractual right to demand the sale arises.
material_facts: The purchaser became entitled to demand an auction only after the owner obtained possession.
By the time the owner obtained possession, the land was no longer subject to the tenant-protection statute invoked by the purchaser.
A separate restriction on alienation operated for a limited period and expired; the contract predated that restriction.
issues.conclusion: The cited land statutes did not prevent enforcement of the contractual obligation to sell the property by auction.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the relevant right to demand an auction arose when the owner obtained possession, at which time the tenant-protection statute no longer applied to the land. A temporary prohibition on alienation did not make an earlier contract incapable of performance after the prohibition expired.

predicates.contract_enforcement_suit: A person brings a proceeding to enforce a contractual obligation concerning land.
predicates.auction_right_arises_after_owner_gets_po: The contract makes the right to demand an auction arise only after the owner obtains possession of the land.
predicates.land_restriction_no_longer_applies_when_: The land restriction invoked against enforcement has ceased to apply to the land or has expired by the time the contractual right to demand the auction arises.

issues.definition: A contractual auction obligation is not barred by a land restriction that no longer applies when the right to demand the auction arises.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should mould an existing decree to comply with a subsequent statutory restriction when doing so can preserve the rights already secured by the decree and avoid futile relief.
material_facts: A decree requiring sale of the property had been passed before a later law restricted transfers of certain land.
The restriction required prescribed steps or an exemption before the land could be transferred.
A scheme for residential premises for weaker sections could be submitted to seek an exemption, and the Court appointed a receiver to take the necessary steps.
The Court modified the decree to provide for the receiver's work and distribution of the proceeds while preserving the parties' rights under the decree.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was dismissed, but the decree was modified to conform to the later law by providing for a receiver to seek the required exemption and implement a qualifying scheme, with the proceeds applied as directed by the Court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, including sections 5(3), 20, and 21. It held that later events and changes in law during an appeal must be considered to do complete justice and avoid a futile decree, and that a decree should be moulded to conform to subsequent law where this can preserve rights obtained under the decree. The Court relied on Pasupuleti Venkateswarlu v. The Motor & General Traders and Rameshwar v. Jot Ram.

predicates.appeal_against_existing_decree: A party appeals against a decree that has already granted relief.
predicates.later_law_restricts_decree_performance: A law that comes into effect after the decree restricts the performance of the relief granted.
predicates.lawful_mechanism_can_preserve_decree_rig: A lawful procedure or arrangement can accommodate the later restriction while preserving the rights secured by the decree.

issues.definition: On appeal, when later law restricts performance but a lawful mechanism can preserve the decree's rights, the decree is adjusted to comply with that law.
